messages:
alice_acme: Hey team — we've seen a spike in 503s and ~600ms tail latency on requests that should be routed to us-west. Traces show they went to eu-west-1 instead. Happening after we upgraded our client SDK yesterday. :grimacing:

sasha_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro request (headers + query) and a couple of request IDs? Also roughly how many requests are affected?

alice_acme: Minimal repro below. We noticed it when the client sent region in two places (header + query) and sometimes as a comma list. About ~2% of requests in the last hour. Request IDs: r-8a3f2, r-8a3f9.

curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" 
  -H "X-Client-Region: us-west-2, eu-west-1" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west-2" 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'

We've also seen variants where the SDK sends the header twice: two separate X-Client-Region headers (us-west-2 and eu-west-1). When that happens the request sometimes lands in EU.

devin_eng: Thanks for the repro. This looks like the classic "multiple region indicators" edge-case. Quick summary from infra: our router has two codepaths — the edge proxy (nginx-ish layer) and the backend router service. The edge proxy historically concatenates duplicate headers into a comma-separated list; our backend router currently parses region by splitting on comma *and* also respects multiple header occurrences but due to a platform mismatch we can end up honoring the wrong position (we pick the last entry in some deployments). In short: when a client sends both a query param and multiple header values, the precedence is ambiguous and can flip depending on which component sees the request first. :eyes:

Workarounds (short term):
- Send a single explicit region param in the querystring: `?region=us-west-2` (we treat explicit query param as highest precedence in new SDKs).
- Avoid sending duplicate X-Client-Region headers or comma lists.
- Upgrade to SDK v0.9.4 which sets `X-Redwood-Preferred-Region` (new header) to avoid the old parsing path.

sasha_support: For customers who can't upgrade immediately: you can add an explicit header `X-Redwood-Force-Region: us-west-2` (our routers currently prefer Force-Region if present) as a stop-gap. I'll paste a one-line curl for ops: 

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -H "X-Redwood-Force-Region: us-west-2" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hi"}'

alice_acme: Thanks — we'll push the header change and schedule the SDK upgrade. Any chance for a billing/latency credit for the affected window? We had a degraded UX and increased compute across ocean.

sasha_support: Please DM me the approximate token counts and we can review for a goodwill credit. If you want I can open a formal claim.

leo_oncall: FYI — I've created an internal issue and assigned to @devin_eng: https://redwood.internal/issues/INC-5482 . Root cause: inconsistent header parsing between edge and router.

devin_eng: Patch landed to normalize duplicate-region handling (we now canonicalize to the first non-empty explicit input with query param > X-Redwood-Force-Region > X-Client-Region list). Deployed to edge fleet at 1951240200. Monitoring for error rate and misroutes.

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: edge-router v1.12.7 -> stable (deploy id: dpl-84219) at 1951240200 :white_check_mark:

sasha_support: Closing loop with the customer — please confirm after your header change. We'll keep INC-5482 open until we see 1 hour of stable traffic.

alice_acme: Confirmed — after adding X-Redwood-Force-Region our traffic routes correctly to us-west and 503s dropped. Thanks all.
